name: Feedback Control of Mechanical Systems
summary: Designing controllers that make machines behave as intended: stability, PID, root locus, frequency-domain and state-space design, and implementation.

topics.name: Open- vs closed-loop control; benefits and costs of feedback
Performance specifications: transient response and steady-state error
PID control and practical tuning (Ziegler-Nichols, anti-windup)
Frequency-response design: Bode and Nyquist plots, gain and phase margins
State-space control: controllability, observability, pole placement, observers
Digital control: sampling, discretisation and z-transform basics
Motion control: feedforward, trajectory tracking, cascaded position/velocity loops
Nonlinearities: saturation, backlash and friction compensation
Introduction to optimal (LQR) and model predictive control
Introduction to robust, adaptive and nonlinear control
Implementation on hardware and hardware-in-the-loop testing
